sentences: Every interpolated pixel input in this build is **perspective-correct at the pixel center**, and every other input is flat, so the single v0/v1 pair the code reads is `PERSP_CENTER`.
The translator models exactly these two: Flat for `v_interp_mov_f32`, plain (perspective, center) inputs and `BaryCoordKHR` for `v_interp_p1/p2` and the f16 forms.

Two records describe each input, and they state **different facts**: PSV0 (DXBC) stores the interpolation **mode**; the FSSM input record's flags byte (byte 7) stores the **read method** — bit 0 (0x01) marks `v_interp_mov_f32` (4,600 records), bit 1 (0x02) 32-bit `v_interp_p1/p2` (51,191; values 0 and 3 never occur), bit 3 (0x08) a Float16-typed parameter (11,619), bit 4 (0x10) the `*_f16` opcodes (11,199; 24 f16-read records lack it).

The flag/usage cross-table over all 55,791 records has no contradiction: every bit-0 position the code reads is read only by `v_interp_mov_f32` (4,295 positions), every bit-1 position only by `v_interp_p1/p2` or the f16 forms (49,594), and no position is read both ways (1,902 positions are unread, and 88 reads fall past the table).

**The mode is in PSV0, not the FSSM**: `tools/ps_interp_modes.py` decodes it from the PSV0 signature elements (`DXIL::InterpolationMode`, "must match D3D_INTERPOLATION_MODE": 1 Constant, 2 Linear, 3 LinearCentroid, 4 LinearNoperspective, 5 LinearNoperspectiveCentroid, 6 LinearSample, 7 LinearNoperspectiveSample; the 16-byte elements carry row, cols, semantic kind, component type and the mode — layout in the Pixel-shader inputs section) and maps the modes onto the `SPI_PS_INPUT_ENA` barycentric-pair bits (Mesa `gfx103.json` register type SPI_PS_INPUT_ENA: PERSP_SAMPLE/CENTER/CENTROID = bits 0/1/2, LINEAR_SAMPLE/CENTER/CENTROID = bits 4/5/6; the same type serves `SPI_PS_INPUT_ADDR`).

**No FSSM word stores ENA/ADDR**: every u16 in bytes 0x00–0x138 of all 12,101 PS was compared against the signature-reconstructed ENA and only constant coincidences matched, and the register addresses (0x286CC/0x286D0, or 0xA1B3/0xA1B4 as context-register indices) appear in no PS blob, so the v2.. position layout of "PS system inputs" (one enabled pair) is the only ENA witness.

Census (12,101 PS; 101,024 declared / 77,245 read inputs): every arbitrary, clip and cull input is Constant (6,333 rows, 4,529 read) or Linear = perspective-centre (81,385 rows, attributes plus 1,806 `SV_ClipDistance` and 2 `SV_CullDistance`); zero centroid, sample or noperspective generics; per shader 6,350 linear only, 4,507 linear and constant, 6 constant only, 1,238 no interpolated input. 101,024 declared / 76,215 read inputs): every arbitrary, clip and cull input is Constant (6,333 rows, 3,652 read) or Linear = perspective-centre (81,385 rows, attributes plus 1,806 `SV_ClipDistance` and 2 `SV_CullDistance`); zero centroid, sample or noperspective generics; per shader 6,350 linear only, 4,507 linear and constant, 6 constant only, 1,238 no interpolated input.
ISG1 has no mode field, and the DXIL part carries no bitcode.
SV_Position is mode 4 (11,295 rows) or mode 5 (27) — noperspective by the D3D rule —.
With packed-component read masks, the classifier assigns 10,260 shaders to the perspective-centre pair and 1,841 to no pair.
It assigns none to a linear pair.
This count measures input classification; it does not directly measure how the hardware delivers SV_Position; front face is a system input (1,984 rows, 345 read, at most one per shader).

SV_Position is mode 4 (11,295 rows) or mode 5 (27) — noperspective by the D3D rule — and is delivered through the system VGPRs in every shader except **4**, which interpolate it through the parameter cache with the *linear* pair (`FragCoord` stays at the pixel center, which only differs at partly covered MSAA pixels); front face is a system input (1,984 rows, 345 read, at most one per shader).

The code reads **one** barycentric pair per shader: v0/v1 in 10,259, none in 1,841, and one shader reads J from v14 (a copy of v1), so the perspective-centre assumption holds for every interpolated generic input.

**Mode and read method disagree in thousands of rows** — the residual surface for modelling is: those 4 linear-pair position shaders, Constant rows read via `p1/p2` or `*_f16` (2,190 records at the matching table position; flat semantics in hardware, not modelled), and Linear rows read only by `v_interp_mov_f32` (3,197; already declared `Flat`).

The translator's table check (`check_read_methods`, the row below) compares each read's opcode against the record's read-method bits (`fssm_header.read_methods`) — since the bits restate the read method, it rejects 0 of 12,101 PS: a consistency check between the two encodings of the read, not a mode check (a centroid/sample/noperspective input would still read `v_interp_p1/p2` and pass; that every interpolated input is perspective-centre is the PSV0 census result above, so keying a refusal on genuinely unmodelled modes means decoding PSV0, not reading these bits).

Counted with `tools/ps_interp_modes.py` (stdlib; PSV0, FSSM and disassembly in one pass; #1301 removed the earlier #1246 census tool in favour of it) on the 1.0.2.1 corpus; tests `tests/test_ps_interp_modes.py`, `tests/test_fssm_header.py` and `tests/test_rdna2spirv_pixelinput.py` (synthetic).
No GPU test: no shader needs centroid or sample interpolation.
**Not covered:** bit 3 (0x08) is set in 11,619 records (all 11,199 16-bit ones, 396 flat, 24 linear).
The 213 PS that overwrite v0/v1 before a `v_interp` (SHADER-178) compute their own barycentrics in code; PSV0 gives them no other mode.
